disclaimer: Analysis and opinion, not investment advice.
precision: day: an ISO date; month: the month is known; window: the first business day of a window; signal: no date, the test resolves on a signal.
specification: resolver.specState approved: the resolver carries question (one binary question), source {label, url} (the official public place the answer appears), rule (how the answer resolves the test) and ambiguity (what happens if the source is late, revised or silent), approved by the owner, or derived for a dated series test from the series and the expression it evaluates; confirmed means the answer to the question is yes; pending: the words are not yet written and those fields are empty. From version 2 the resolver also carries specVersion, specUpdatedOn and specHistory. A row with sameAs is the same question as that test: its resolver is a copy, its status and resultId mirror the parent, and it has no result of its own. Since 10 October 2026 a resolver may carry callExpects (yes, no or either: the answer the Part's Call expected when the words were approved) and every row carries stage: pre (the words approved on or before the test's date), post (after it; such a test is counted and never rated) or open (no words yet).
stageRule: Pre-specified means the words were approved on or before the test’s date. Specified after the date means they were written afterwards: such a test is counted and shown, and never rated. An open question has no words yet.
callExpectsRule: callExpects records which answer the Call expected when the words of a test were approved: yes, no, or either when the Call stakes nothing on the answer; a result supports the Call when the answer was the one expected, weakens it when it was the other, and informs it when either answer was foreseen.

The federal price data for August: whether the median twelve-month rise in household prices across PJM's nine jurisdictions stays at least four points above the median of the other 42, from 11.7% against 5.6% in July.

resolver.rule: The price is residential revenue divided by residential sales over September 2025 to August 2026, against September 2024 to August 2025, for each of the 51 jurisdictions, as the Part computes it for the year to July (11.7% against 5.6%). Confirmed if the PJM median minus the median of the other 42 is 4.0 points or more; refuted if it is below 4.0 points.
resolver.question: In the EIA-861M data through August 2026, as first published, is the median twelve-month change in the average household price per kilowatt-hour across the nine jurisdictions PJM serves (Delaware, the District of Columbia, Illinois, Maryland, New Jersey, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia) at least four percentage points above the median change across the other 42?

source.label: U.S. Energy Information Administration, EIA-861M monthly sales and revenue (first release of the month tested)

resolver.ambiguity: Data for August not published by November 15, 2026 is inconclusive. Figures are read as first published in that release; later revisions do not reopen the test. If EIA withholds the residential figures for more than two of the nine PJM jurisdictions, the test is inconclusive, reviewed by the owner.

This test decides only the price leg of the second exit from the house's view; the rule on large loads bringing their own capacity is read separately in the story.
